why: The doc quote is real (subagents.md line 179, the only 'effort' occurrence on the page; identical modulo one space of table padding, and the row is a single cell with no reversing second sentence). The cited identifiers are real too: definitions.ts:89 `effort?: ThinkingLevel`, :403 `normalizeThinkingLevel(entry.effort)`, :453 the conditional spread, thinking-levels.ts:146-150 returning undefined for anything outside off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is false in the exact shape this repo's audit history warns about: the evidence list cites :403 and :453 and skips the eleven lines between them. definitions.ts:424-425 is `if (entry.effort !== undefined && effort === undefined) throw new Error("Invalid ${label}.effort")`. A numeric effort is therefore REJECTED, loudly and by name, not silently dropped. The conditional spread at :453 is never reached with a bad value. Verified empirically with a positive control: a config carrying `{name:'numeric', effort: 5}` yields `DEFS: []` and `FAILURES: [{reason: "Invalid orchestratorAgents[0].effort"}]`, while the control `{effort: 'high'}` loads as `{n:'named', e:'high'}`. The same throw guards every other effort entry point — pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:326-327 (descriptor path) and :593-596 (markdown-frontmatter path) — so there is no path on which a numeric effort is silently discarded. definitions.test.ts:213-241 pins this as designed fail-closed behavior, listing `{ effort: 'ultra' }` among the malformed ceilings that must refuse the entry with a named reason. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) and not a branding/subscription-flow product difference. A residual divergence does exist — Claude's union admits `number` and ours does not — but the finding as written misstates both the mechanism and its user-visible effect, and its actual effect is materially different (whole-agent refusal, not a dropped field), so the row is refuted rather than confirmed.
correctedState: AgentDefinition.effort is typed `ThinkingLevel` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:89) and parsed by normalizeThinkingLevel (packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts:146-150), which returns undefined for anything outside off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max — including a number. A numeric effort is NOT silently dropped: definitions.ts:424-425 throws `Invalid <label>.effort`, and readUserAgentDefinitions reports that as a named per-entry failure so the ENTIRE agent definition fails to load (measured: `effort: 5` -> zero definitions plus `Invalid orchestratorAgents[0].effort`; `effort: 'high'` -> loads). The markdown-frontmatter and runtime-descriptor paths throw the same way (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:326-327 and :593-596), and the fail-closed refusal is pinned by definitions.test.ts:213-241. The real divergence from the doc is narrower than claimed: Claude's `effort` union admits `number`, ours admits only the named levels, and a Claude AgentDefinition carrying a numeric effort is rejected outright rather than coerced or ignored.
